**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Probe writability when the target directory already exists**

When `$WT_TARGET` already exists but is not writable, such as after an ownership change or when the volume becomes read-only, `mkdir -p "$WT_TARGET"` returns success without creating anything. The script therefore selects the managed branch, can publish or retain a symlink to that directory, and exits successfully even though Cargo cannot write to `target/`. The new fallback needs a probe that actually creates an entry inside the target directory, not merely an idempotent `mkdir -p` of the directory itself.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

RED-VERIFIED: cargo_target_link_falls_back_when_the_existing_worktree_dir_is_unwritable

Correct, and it was the sharper half of the bug. `mkdir -p` on an existing directory succeeds without touching it, so an existing worktree directory that had gone read-only passed the probe and received a symlink Cargo could not write into. The probe now creates an entry inside the directory (mktemp) and removes it -- the operation Cargo actually needs, and one root cannot fake past EROFS.

The test uses a FRESH checkout: with a pre-existing target/, the script's own "retaining unmanaged local target/" exit fires first and hides exactly this defect -- the first draft of the test made that mistake and passed. Against the previous commit's script: FAILED (symlink published to the unwritable dir). With the create-probe: fallback to a local target/, 32/32.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Lock the generation before creating the write probe**

When the disk preflight has already exclusively locked `$WT_TARGET`, these lines still create and remove a directory entry without taking the generation lease. `prune-cargo-target.sh` performs a census and then rewalks the locked tree; a probe appearing after the census has no census record, while one disappearing during the rewalk triggers `target entry disappeared during reclaim`, so an ordinary concurrent `make` can abort the hourly preflight and its job. Acquire the same generation lock before probing the directory.

RED-VERIFIED: cargo_target_link_does_not_touch_a_generation_it_has_not_leased

Correct, and it is the ZERO RACE CONDITIONS rule exactly. The probe now runs inside the lease block, after the exclusive lease on the candidate generation and before the retirement check, so the pruner's census/rewalk can never observe it; the early `mkdir -p` stays because creating the generation directory is outside any tree the pruner walks.

The test is the pruner: LOCK_EX on the generation directory, the script under `timeout 4`, and the directory's mtime must be untouched when the timeout fires. Against the previous commit the script blocked at the lease (exit 124) but the mtime had moved -- the probe had run outside the lock. Now it blocks with the mtime unchanged.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Replace an existing unwritable managed target during fallback**

When `target` already points to a managed directory that later becomes unwritable, the new probe correctly sets `btrfs_usable=0`, but this branch only prints the warning and leaves the symlink intact. Because the link still resolves, the dangling-link repair is skipped and the final `-d target` check succeeds; the script exits 0 even though Cargo cannot create files there. This occurs with the ownership-change and read-only-remount cases described above, so the fallback must also repoint or replace an existing managed symlink after safely leasing it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

RED-VERIFIED: cargo_target_link_replaces_a_managed_link_to_an_unwritable_dir

Correct: warning and walking away left a link that resolves, so every later `-d target` check passed while Cargo could not create a file. One fallback_to_local now serves every give-up path and REPLACES a managed symlink with a real local directory -- safe under the checkout lock plus the exclusive lease on that generation that the script already holds -- and fails closed if no usable directory results. A fresh generation that cannot be created takes the same path instead of dying under set -e.

Against the previous commit: exit 0 with the symlink left in place. Now: a real, usable local target/.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Detect mount capability before using the root-only fixture**

When the tests run as UID 0 without `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, as in a standard unprivileged Docker container, `nix_geteuid_is_root()` selects this branch even though the bind mount is forbidden. I checked this in the supplied root container, where `mount --bind` returned `permission denied`, so this assertion fails before exercising the script; `cargo_target_link_replaces_a_managed_link_to_an_unwritable_dir` repeats the same assumption. Detect whether the mount operation is available and use a non-mount fallback when it is not.

RED-VERIFIED: cargo_target_link_falls_back_when_the_existing_worktree_dir_is_unwritable and cargo_target_link_replaces_a_managed_link_to_an_unwritable_dir, on the new fixture.

Correct: as UID 0 without CAP_SYS_ADMIN the bind remount is refused and the test died before reaching the script. Rather than detect the capability and keep two fixtures, one fixture now serves every uid: the managed worktree directory is a symlink into procfs, where creating an entry is refused for root and non-root alike -- `mkdir -p` succeeds (it exists), the lease fd opens, and the write probe inside the lease fails. No mount, no capability. The fixture asserts on itself that a write is really refused, so it cannot go vacuous.

Both tests fail against the script from two commits back (mkdir-only probe) and pass with the current one; 34/34.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify writability before accepting the local fallback**

When creating `$WT_TARGET` fails and an existing local `target/` is also unwritable, this branch only warns and falls through to the final directory-type check, so the script exits 0 even though Cargo still cannot write. For example, running as a non-root user with both the btrfs stand-in and an existing local `target/` set to mode 0555 returns success, while creating `target/probe` fails with `Permission denied`; probe the retained local target before reporting a successful fallback.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

RED-VERIFIED: cargo_target_link_refuses_an_unwritable_local_target_when_btrfs_is_unusable, cargo_target_link_refuses_an_unwritable_local_target_on_managed_fallback, every_local_target_exit_probes_writability_first (tests/test_cargo_target_link.rs)

One probe, `require_writable_local_target` (mkdir if absent, `-d`, then `mktemp` inside it), now runs at every exit that leaves target/ as a plain local directory: `fallback_to_local`, the unmanaged-target retention, and the script's fall-through end (6ae47ade). A target/ that passes `-d` but cannot be written exits 1 with `target/ is a directory nothing can write`.

Watched failing against the previous head: both behavioural tests (target/ pointing at /proc/self, which no uid can create in, with the volume unusable in one and the managed dir unwritable in the other) got exit 0 from the script, and the structural pin found `exit 0` lines with no probe. All pass on 6ae47ade. The retained-real-directory exit is the one covered structurally rather than driven: as uid 0 it needs a mount or `chattr +i`, and overlayfs in the container lane refuses the flag (`chattr: Operation not permitted`).

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Lease managed targets on the unusable-volume path**

When `$WT_TARGET` is absent or cannot be created but `target` still resolves to an existing `$WT_TARGET.generation-*` directory, such as when a rotated generation remains after the canonical directory is removed and its parent becomes read-only, `btrfs_usable` stays zero and the block that acquires `old_target_lease_fd` is skipped. This final call then creates and removes its probe through the managed link without a generation lease, so a concurrent `prune-cargo-target.sh` census or rewalk can abort; if that generation is also unwritable, the script exits 1 instead of replacing the link with a local target. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier fixed probe path is that the `btrfs_usable == 0` fallthrough never opens a generation lease, so lease and remove a retained managed link before probing the local fallback.

RED-VERIFIED: cargo_target_link_drops_a_managed_link_it_cannot_lease (tests/test_cargo_target_link.rs)

The unusable-volume branch now calls `drop_managed_link` (shared with `fallback_to_local`) before the final probe: a `target/` that resolves into `$BTRFS_ROOT/cargo-target/` is unlinked and a local `target/` takes its place; the generation itself is never touched, so nothing is created or removed inside a directory this run holds no lease on, and an unwritable generation no longer turns into an exit 1 (55892ace).

Watched failing against 6ae47ade: `$WT_TARGET` staged as a dangling symlink (so `mkdir -p` fails for every uid, root included), `target/` pointing at a retained `.generation-stale000` directory with its mtime pinned to 1600000000. The script exited 0 with `target/` still the managed link and the generation's mtime changed by the probe file. Passes on 55892ace: the link is gone, `target/` is a writable local directory, the generation's mtime is unchanged.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fall back when the candidate lease cannot be opened**

When an existing `$WT_TARGET` loses read permission as well as write permission, for example after an ownership change leaves a fresh checkout's directory mode 0700, `mkdir -p` succeeds but `exec {candidate_lease_fd}<"$candidate"` exits under `set -e` before this new probe runs. The script therefore still fails instead of creating the promised local target; handle failure to open the lease as an unusable managed target and add an inaccessible-directory regression case before resolving.

When `--rotate` is used, `target` is a writable unmanaged symlink, and the managed candidate cannot be written, this unconditional fallback retains the unmanaged link and exits 0. I checked the `make clean` invocation in the Makefile: the linked directory's payload remains present even though clean reports success, whereas the existing unusable-volume branch correctly rejects an unrotatable local target. Make this fallback reject rotation unless it actually replaces the target with an empty namespace, and add a failing regression case.
